question.:question/problem: Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{-5x-4}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-5x-4.$ Then $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}={u}^{-1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-5.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (-5) \\  & =\frac{5}{2\sqrt{(-5x-4{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Radical Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{-6x+33}+4{x}^{3}$ at the point where $x=4.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Let $f(x)=\sqrt{-6x+33}.$ We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-6x+33.$ Then $f=\sqrt{u}={u}^{1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-1/2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-6.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-6) \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{u}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{-6x+33}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=-\frac{3}{\sqrt{-6x+33}}+12x^{2}.
$$

Finally, substituting $x=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4} & =-\frac{6}{2\sqrt{-6(4)+33}}+12(4)^{2} \\  & =-1+192 \\  & =191.\end{aligned}
$$
